items.title: deadmau5's AUTO/PILOT Just Landed in Public Beta: A New Power Tool for DJs and Live Performers?
items.excerpt: deadmau5 has pushed his AUTO/PILOT DJ and live-performance platform into public beta, pitching an assisted, stem-aware performance rig rather than a conventional deck layout. It puts an artist-built AI performance tool in front of working DJs for the first time.

items.title: Can Google Build the All-in-One AI Music Studio?
items.excerpt: Google's Flow Music Spaces update folds song generation, editing, stem splitting and video creation into a single AI workspace. It moves Google from a prompt-to-song toy toward something producers could treat as a session environment.

items.title: Watch out, Suno: Google upgrades Lyria AI with 'more realistic vocals'
items.excerpt: Google DeepMind's upgraded Lyria model rolls out inside Flow Music with structural awareness of verse/chorus/bridge, more expressive vocals and finer tempo and duration control. The vocal and arrangement gains are the part that changes what creators can actually use.

items.title: I tested 9 of the best stem separation tools. Here's how they compare
items.excerpt: MusicTech runs nine AI stem separation tools through the same material to compare artefacts, speed and DAW integration. A practical map of which unmixing model to trust for remix, sampling and live work.

items.title: Beatbox your ideas into reality with Vochlea's DubBox, an app that converts your voice into drum loops
items.excerpt: Vochlea's DubBox listens to beatboxing and turns it into a finished drum loop, using voice as the input device instead of pads or a grid. It is a small but concrete shift in how an idea gets from a producer's head into a session.

items.title: Fender CEO clarifies his controversial comments comparing cover songs to AI
items.excerpt: Edward 'Bud' Cole walks back his description of cover music as 'analogue AI' after musicians pushed back, while still arguing AI can help players learn. A live argument about where imitation ends and authorship begins for instrument makers.

items.title: Empire Of The Sun's Luke Steele says 'of course' he uses AI
items.excerpt: Luke Steele describes AI as already inside his writing process and warns artists who refuse it that it will 'swallow you'. A working-artist counterpoint to the refusal stance dominating the AI-music conversation.

items.title: Saregama, India's oldest label, is using AI to make music videos for songs whose visuals it never owned
items.excerpt: Saregama is generating AI music videos for catalog songs whose original visuals it never controlled, repackaging a century-old archive for Gen Z feeds. A concrete production pipeline for AI video attached to real catalog, not a demo.

items.title: Why have we yet to hear an AI-generated hit?
items.excerpt: MIDiA argues generative models can already produce catchy, even beautiful songs, yet none has become a genuine hit — and asks what is missing beyond raw audio quality. A useful frame for what human craft still supplies.

items.title: Quiet Riot, Ozzy bassist Rudy Sarzo on How He Uses AI
items.excerpt: Rudy Sarzo details how he uses AI tools to create new music and why he sees them as instruments rather than replacements. A veteran session player's workflow account rather than a policy opinion.

items.title: Good News! Spotify Removed 75 Million AI-Generated Slop Music Tracks
items.excerpt: Spotify's new filter has stripped 75 million fully AI-generated, impersonation and mass-upload tracks that were siphoning royalties. It sets a de facto quality line that creators uploading AI-assisted work now have to stay on the right side of.

items.title: Startup SoundGate launches an 'AI tutor' for learning guitar
items.excerpt: SoundGate's first product is an AI-powered guitar tutor that listens to a player and coaches in real time. Music education is becoming a design surface for real-time audio models, not just generation.

items.title: Tyga Admits to Making New Album $tarface With AI: 'I Don't Care'
items.excerpt: Tyga openly says he used AI across his new album and compares it to the arrival of Auto-Tune. A mainstream artist normalising generative tools as production craft rather than hiding them.

items.title: Suno CEO insists Suno is 'responsible' and isn't going to leave people behind
items.excerpt: Suno's CEO frames the platform as an extension of music's long history with technology and previews transparency tools for identifying AI-generated songs. The framing shapes how the biggest generative music tool positions itself to creators.

items.title: Sarah's Voice | Creating Art With Her Own Voice
items.excerpt: ElevenLabs profiles Sarah, an artist living with MND who uses a model of her own voice to keep making work and speak for underrepresented communities. Voice cloning shown as authorship preservation rather than impersonation.

items.title: How AI Agents Are Quietly Automating Music Companies
items.excerpt: Agents are taking over delivery QC, metadata, A&R scanning and release ops inside music companies, with a sober read on what actually works. It maps which parts of a creative team's day are already being handed to software.

items.title: What if AI's biggest impact on music isn't just what gets made, but what gets wanted?
items.excerpt: Sammy Andrews argues the real AI fight in music is over discovery and demand shaping, not only over who owns the output. It reframes AI as a taste-formation layer that creators design against.

items.title: Fenix Flexin isn't even denying using AI to make 'Rubberz' anymore
items.excerpt: The rapper's story shifts from denial to 'never said I didn't' as evidence mounts that a charting hit came out of the AI generator Treblo. The disclosure norm for AI-made records is being set in public, song by song.
